## 固定收益開篇論述

聯準會主席凱文・華許在首次傑克森霍爾演說中表示，通膨並未明顯放緩、金融情勢稱不上具有限制性，聯準會2%的目標也維持不變。美國公債因而在8月28日遭到拋售，殖利率曲線大幅趨平。2年期殖利率上升11.2個基點至4.345%，5年期上升8個基點至4.48%，10年期上升4.3個基點至4.72%，30年期則上升1.2個基點至5.207%。

這次賣壓集中在短天期，與華許7月記者會後由長端領跌的行情不同。2年與10年期利差收窄6.9個基點至37.5個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄10個基點至86.2個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升5.8個基點至2.402%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降1.5個基點至2.318%。這代表投資人上調的是經通膨調整後的政策利率預期路徑，而不是要求整條殖利率曲線提供更多通膨補償。

華許並未承諾在9月15至16日的會議升息。他表示自己遵循的是政策紀律，而非預先鎖定某項決定，並延續對例行前瞻指引的反對立場。不過，他提出的標準是基礎通膨必須以足夠速度明確朝2%移動，比市場從7月訊息中理解的條件更嚴格。聯邦基金期貨顯示，9月升息機率由演說前約36%升至50%以上，年底前至少升息一次則幾乎完全反映在價格中。巴克萊也從原先預期2026年不升息，改為預測9月與12月各升息25個基點。

演說前後公布的一系列疲弱經濟數據，並未扭轉這波重新定價。8月芝加哥採購經理人指數由57.6降至47.1，遠低於58.3的市場共識。非農就業年度基準初估將3月就業人數下修7.9萬人，並非經濟學家原先預期的上修，民間就業下修幅度更大。密西根大學消費者信心仍低於7月，家庭短期通膨預期也遭下修。這些數據使下次決策仍取決於後續資訊，卻未取代華許對目前政策限制力仍不足的判斷。

跨資產市場也反映更高的預期實質利率路徑。美元指數上漲0.52%，黃金期貨大跌2.85%至$4,478.10。利率敏感的科技股回吐前一交易日部分漲幅，S&P 500下跌0.27%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.71%，半導體指數重挫3.48%。VIX仍小幅降至14.42，顯示這是有序的重新定價，而非市場普遍搶進避險部位。WTI與布蘭特原油亦溫和下跌，限制當日能源價格的推升作用；投資級、高收益與新興市場債券基金價格則小幅走低。

公債市場的反應緩解了一項長端疑慮，也就是市場對聯準會抗通膨決心的懷疑，但並未消除資本需求本身。美國債務已超過$40兆，AI投資持續帶來大規模公共與民間融資；即使殖利率曲線趨平，長天期殖利率仍處高檔。海外方面，日本2年期公債標售需求疲弱、歐洲通膨加速，加上個別信用事件承壓，均顯示多個市場正同時面對政策趨緊預期與龐大融資需求。

## 成長訊號轉弱之際，Warsh重定價政策路徑

華許最重要的改變並非明確主張9月升息，而是更清楚說明需要維持限制性政策的條件。他重申，2%通膨目標以個人消費支出物價指數衡量，而且目標固定不變，回應了他7月似乎未排除更換通膨衡量基準所引發的疑慮。他也指出，近期較有利的CPI與PCE數據，尚不足以證明基礎通膨趨勢已有實質改善。

更強烈的政策訊號來自華許對金融情勢的評估。他表示，廣泛金融情勢很難被形容為具有限制性，等於挑戰了另一種主張：只要將聯邦基金利率維持在3.5%至3.75%，即使不再升息，也能逐步壓低需求。他同時稱短期利率是聯準會履行法定職責的主要工具，降低了先前討論多項政策工具所造成的模糊空間。

這套框架使華許的立場更接近早已支持緊縮的官員。7月決策有3名具投票權成員持異議，主張升息25個基點；另有數名官員支持升息，許多人也表示，若通膨未能下降，就有必要收緊政策。華許並未採用他們的升息時程，但相較於等待的理由，他更重視物價穩定，並認為就業大致符合充分就業狀態。

債市補上了政策論述未明說的結論。2年期殖利率上升11.2個基點，是各基準天期中最大漲幅，30年期則幾乎未動。這種走勢與市場預期近期將採取政策行動一致，因為更快收緊政策可降低通膨日後持續失控的部分風險。2年與30年期利差收窄10個基點，也幾乎追平演說後盤中所見的曲線平坦化幅度。

不過，長天期債券以收盤價計算並未上漲。30年期殖利率收在5.207%，仍較一個月前高11.7個基點；10年期同期也上升11.3個基點。即使立場更強硬的聯準會可降低部分期限溢價，財政舉債、偏高的能源成本，以及企業發債帶來的資金競爭，仍要求投資人持有長天期債券時取得可觀補償。

交易資料顯示，這波重新定價發生在活躍的現券市場。FINRA記錄的名目附息債券面額成交量達$1.17兆，較前一日增加19.1%。2年期以下債券成交量增加36.5%，逾5年至7年以下的附息債券成交量增加30.3%，TIPS成交量更增加84%。這些數字是雙向交易量，不能用來判斷買賣方向，但可看出調整最集中於對政策重估最敏感的區段。

經濟數據使政策訊號更複雜，卻沒有將其推翻。芝加哥PMI降至47.1，代表景氣由擴張驟然轉為收縮，且低於所有既有比較基準，包括前值57.6、市場共識58.3及預測56.1。8月31日公布的達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數，市場預期由-6升至-5，將成為下一項區域性檢驗，用以判斷這波疲弱是局部現象，還是更廣泛工業放緩的一環。

就業基準修正的整體幅度小於前一次年度調整，卻揭示民間部門放緩更為明顯。3月非農就業初估下修7.9萬人、即0.1%；前一次年度修正為下修91.1萬人，而本次調查原先預期上修18.3萬人。最新調整幅度也低於過去10年平均0.2%的絕對修正幅度。

組成細節比總數更值得警惕。民間就業下修17.8萬人，其中製造業減少6.7萬人，貿易、運輸與公用事業減少9.8萬人；政府就業則上修9.9萬人，抵銷總數中大部分民間部門下修。這項基準修正意味，截至3月止一年內的平均每月就業成長較接近1.1萬人，而非先前公布的1.76萬人。最終數據將於2027年2月隨2027年1月就業報告公布。

消費者數據同樣顯示動能轉弱，但尚不足以解除通膨警報。密西根大學8月消費者信心終值為51.7，高於初步共識51，卻低於7月的55.2。一年期通膨預期由4.2%下修至4%，低於預期的4.3%，但水準仍高；5年期預期維持3.3%，與前值及市場共識相同。因此，家庭並不像初步調查所顯示的那麼悲觀，但無論信心或長期通膨預期，都尚未回到令人安心的水準。

每週石油鑽井數由452座降至447座，低於市場共識454座。鑽井數減少無法決定短期原油價格，但在中東衝突仍是全球主要能源風險之際，延續了中期供給疑慮。週五WTI下跌0.16%至$83.40，布蘭特下跌0.43%至$89.31，只帶來有限的短期緩解，並未明顯改變通膨背景。

整體而言，市場認為政策行動更具急迫性，但9月結果仍未確定。芝加哥調查與民間就業下修支持審慎行事；家庭5年期通膨預期未變，加上華許認為金融情勢寬鬆，則使升息仍是可行選項。因此，行情反轉風險也偏高：若聯準會再次按兵不動，卻未提出清楚解釋，7月時曾推升曲線陡峭化的公信力疑慮可能重新浮現。

## 日本升息預期壓迫債券與日圓

日本市場透過通膨、標售需求與匯率政策，傳遞出與美國相似的緊縮訊號。8月東京不含生鮮食品的消費者物價年增1.8%，高於前值1.7%，符合預期；不含生鮮食品與能源的通膨率達2%，整體指數則上升1.9%。即使政府措施壓低家庭能源成本，通膨仍然加速。

細項同時反映服務價格壓力與補貼效果。服務價格年增1.4%，租金、餐飲、醫療費用，以及教育與休閒耐久財均有貢獻。不含生鮮食品的食品價格上升3.6%；米價則在一年前大漲68%後下跌14.2%，創2005年5月以來最大跌幅。能源價格整體下跌2%，其中汽油下跌2.7%、電價下跌2.4%，反映政府限制燃料成本，並於7月至9月補貼電力與天然氣。

勞動市場仍然吃緊。7月失業率降至2.4%，求才求職比維持1.18，亦即每100名求職者對應118個職缺。即使管制價格壓低整體物價，服務通膨僵固、勞動力短缺及日圓持續疲弱，仍共同強化日本央行升息預期。

這項預期也反映在2年期日本公債標售。投標倍數由前次3.63降至2.97，遠低於過去12個月平均3.74；標售尾差則由0.007擴大至0.034，創2016年以來最大。對政策敏感的2年期殖利率已由8月初約1.56%升至1.70%，10年期殖利率則來到2.92%，逼近3%。

隔夜指數交換顯示，日本央行9月升息機率約為82%至84%，10月升息則已完全反映在價格中。副總裁氷見野良三先前已警告，基礎通膨若高於2%目標，將損害經濟，也未否定9月升息的可能性。隨著會議接近，標售需求疲弱顯示投資人需要更清楚的政策指引，或要求價格進一步讓利。

財務省隨後公布了支撐日圓的行動規模。日本在7月30日至8月26日間投入¥15.4兆、約$964億，創單月新高。其中包括7月31日美日協調干預匯市，是1998年以來首次聯手支撐日圓。美方投入金額未計入日本數據，但美國參與提高了行動的嚇阻效果。

干預改變了日圓走勢，卻沒有修正根本失衡。日圓在首次行動前接近164兌1美元，8月3日一度升至155.23，之後又於東京週五晚間回貶至約159.68。日本今年已投入約¥27兆干預匯市，日圓仍接近160關卡。美日利差寬廣、油價偏高、財政疑慮，以及日本機構持續投資海外，仍不利日圓持久升值。

因此，未來將有更多調整責任落在貨幣政策上。市場已大幅反映9月單次升息，日圓若要持續回升，投資人必須相信正常化將在下一步之後延續。華許轉趨鷹派則推高美國預期利率路徑，作用方向正好相反，限制了日本央行升息原本可能帶來的匯率支撐。

財政政策也為日本公債需求增添壓力。各部會下一財政年度預算要求可能突破歷史新高的¥130兆，高於本年度初始與追加預算合計約¥125兆。首相高市早苗表示，希望新發債規模低於¥40兆，但融資安排相當吃緊。

在名目成長3%的假設下，稅收原估為¥87.8兆，高於今年預估的¥83.7兆。高市規劃調降食品消費稅，將減少約¥5兆收入，使稅收再度接近¥83兆。即使另加約¥9兆非稅收入，只要支出超過¥130兆，資金缺口仍接近¥40兆。新債若接近此數，即使未突破首相設定的上限，也會高於本財政年度的¥32.7兆。

企業與外國借款人也試圖在利率進一步上升前鎖定日圓融資。日本混合債發行量預計截至9月達約¥1.18兆，為2021財政年度以來最高。Panasonic完成¥1,000億的30年期與30年零1個月次順位債定價，票息分別為3.455%及4.188%，相對JGB利差為110及130個基點。約¥1.32兆的未償混合債預計在2026財政年度進入首次贖回日，與併購融資同時形成再融資需求。

墨西哥相隔2年首次發行武士債，募得¥2,828億，高於2024年8月的¥1,522億。4個券別期限介於3.5年至20年，定價較日圓交換利率高115至210個基點。交易規模顯示日本投資人基礎仍有深度，但借款人趕在日本央行進一步行動前籌資，也增加了投資人必須吸收的供給。

## 歐洲通膨強化9月升息理由

歐洲通膨數據與央行官員談話更一致地指向升息。西班牙8月消費者物價年增4.5%，創2023年以來最快速度，超過歐洲央行目標的兩倍；法國通膨則加速至2.7%，為5月以來最高，也高於預期。與中東衝突相關的能源價格是兩國主要推力。

9月1日公布的歐元區數據預計將由2.9%升至3.3%，同樣是2023年以來最快。核心通膨預料維持2.5%，若結果符合預期，將顯示最新加速仍集中於能源，而非基礎價格普遍再度上升。德國通膨預估為3.1%，義大利則為3.4%。

這些數據將是歐洲央行9月10日決策前最後一批重要物價指標。繼6月首次升息後，投資人已反映再次升息25個基點、將存款利率提高至2.5%的情境。剩餘爭議在於，這一步是否足以阻止能源衝擊傳導至薪資與其他價格。

斯洛維尼亞央行總裁Primoz Dolenc表示，經濟成長優於預期、能源成本居高不下，伊朗衝突亦未顯著改善，因此9月採取行動的理由充分。他承認目前尚未見到明顯的第二輪效應，但認為若等到效應浮現才行動，可能削弱市場對歐洲央行通膨目標的信心。若9月升息，他認為12月發布預測時將是重新評估中期路徑的下一個時點。

拉脫維亞央行總裁Martins Kazaks同樣表示，不能任由高通膨扎根，並稱再次升息有相當可能性。奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher則強調，歐元區經濟動能比預期更強。第2季產出成長0.4%，讓決策官員得以考慮進一步限制政策，而沒有跡象顯示能源衝擊已使經濟停止成長。

英國的立場形成鮮明對比。英格蘭銀行總裁Andrew Bailey表示，通膨的第二輪效應仍受抑制，勞動市場也持續轉弱，官員目前可以先觀察情勢。他在7月30日與另外5名成員組成6比3多數，支持維持利率不變，當時並警告不應把該決定解讀為正在轉向升息。

儘管如此，市場已完全反映英格蘭銀行年底前升息25個基點、明年春季再升一次的情境。英國通膨出現3月以來首次加速，家庭對未來一年物價漲幅的預期也達3.9%。Bailey提出的反向因素是就業疲弱：企業正在裁員，職缺降至5年低點，民間部門薪資成長亦放緩。他並未保證第二輪效應會持續受抑制，因此9月17日的決策仍取決於能源通膨是否擴散至薪資與服務價格。

法國除面臨區域通膨問題，主權信用環境也更為棘手。修正後數據顯示，第1季產出萎縮0.2%，第2季零成長，經濟僅以極小差距避開衰退。與此同時，法國10年期公債相對德國的殖利率溢酬，已由2026年初不到60個基點擴大至約85個基點。

首場總統辯論顯示，各方對如何縮減赤字幾乎沒有共識。Jean-Luc Mélenchon主張協商取消歐洲央行持有的債務；Marine Le Pen則提出縮減政府規模、減少移民，並可能削減對歐盟的出資，以節省€1,250億。Le Pen也保留最快可自60歲退休的年金提案，每年成本約€90億。前總理Edouard Philippe反對取消債務，認為這將威脅法國取得融資的能力。

惠譽維持法國A+評等與穩定展望，讓政府暫時鬆一口氣，但明確的降評風險依然存在。該機構表示，若政治分裂持續，或削減赤字未能取得實質進展，可能先將展望調為負向，之後再調降評等。惠譽預測法國赤字占GDP比率在2026年為5.2%、2027年為5.5%、2028年為5.2%；由於成長轉弱、利息成本上升與國防支出增加，這些預估比先前評估更差。

歐洲央行升息與財政僵局並存，使法國在歐元區內格外脆弱。9月收緊政策或可處理區域通膨，卻也會提高維持財政赤字的成本，而惠譽預期赤字至2028年都將高於GDP的5%。穩定評等避免了立即的評等衝擊，卻無法消除投資人已針對法國國內政治與預算風險要求的溢酬。

## AI融資擴張，信用保障減弱

AI投資正從債務市場幾乎所有區塊吸收資金。Pimco認為，8月稍早10年期美國公債殖利率升向4.75%，部分原因是AI相關發債快速湧入，與政府借款競爭資金。這波投資週期可能提高生產力與成長，但在主權融資需求也同步上升之際，短期現實仍是需要投入大量資本。

SoftBank正尋求另一筆$100億、2年期貸款，利率約為SOFR加275個基點。瑞穗負責安排此案，銀行須在8月31日前承諾額度。募集資金可用來再融資先前為投資OpenAI而取得的$400億過橋貸款。

這筆新借款之外，SoftBank還可能發行最多$200億債券，並已有一筆以OpenAI持股擔保的$100億貸款；其契約條款可能要求提供現金擔保或提前還款。SoftBank預計在10月前向OpenAI投入接近$650億。能夠進入多種市場，可降低對單一投資人群體的依賴，但銀行貸款、擔保借款與潛在債券發行，實際上都在為同一筆高度集中的科技曝險融資。

Lambda透過短天期私募債務籌得約$10億，用以購買將出租給Microsoft的Nvidia繪圖處理器，由JPMorgan安排配售。該公司8月稍早才完成另一筆$9.26億貸款，用於GPU及相關基礎設施。與Microsoft簽訂的協議為設備提供了已知使用者，但這筆融資仍取決於專用晶片的價值、使用率及技術壽命。

Iren取得的融資規模更大、成本也更高。Blue Owl旗下基金主導一筆$24億融資，包括$12億優先擔保定期貸款與$12億優先擔保票據，兩部分利率均為9%，並在撥款後2年半到期。這項安排讓Iren可分階段為加拿大資料中心園區採購Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPU。

短天期尤其值得注意，因為Iren預測2027財政年度資本支出最高可達$300億。分階段採購可以降低立即資金需求，但若債務到期前工程進度、客戶需求或GPU經濟效益發生變化，再融資風險依然存在。Iren在公布財報後，股價週五重挫近13%。

可轉換債發行則顯示，投資人正在接受另一種形式的保障減少。今年全球科技公司可轉換債銷售額已達$1,470億，較2025年同期高逾50%，也已超越2021年創下的歷年全年紀錄。部分新券票息已趨近零，買方愈來愈依賴轉換為股票的選擇權取得報酬。

衡量可轉換債對標的股票敏感度的市場平均delta，已升至約64%，接近2021年以來最高。Nebius上週單獨募得$45億，此前已另發行$97.5億；部分新券票息僅0%至0.5%。利息收益緩衝偏低，意味發行人股價一旦下跌，投資人可能只剩下幾乎不提供當期收益的無擔保債權。

目前情況並非完全重演2021年。與疫情期間發行零息可轉換債的公司相比，若干現有發行人的營收成長與獲利能力更強。然而，股票、信用債與可轉換債投資組合也因此同時集中於AI主題。這是一個生產力正在擴張的產業，還是融資過度的產業，將取決於專案使用率、借款人現金流，以及最終文件中保留多少投資人保障。

信用壓力並非全都來自新建AI設施。Acrisure一筆2030年到期、規模$44億的貸款，8月價格下跌約10點至面額的83美分左右，成為彭博美國槓桿貸款指數中負面貢獻最大的借款人。該公司另一筆$11億、2030年到期的債券一度跌至面額的87美分左右，並成為一項廣泛美國高收益債指數當月第二大拖累。

市場對Acrisure與Guggenheim關係的疑慮，又疊加在營運結果轉弱及槓桿偏高之上。Guggenheim Investments曾代表客戶參與Acrisure在2022年的優先股融資；Acrisure則表示，把這項少數股權投資描述為更廣泛關係的說法具有誤導性。儘管如此，美國當局正在調查Mark Walter金融體系其他部分可能存在的不當行為，雙方關聯仍受到市場關注。

Acrisure本身的基本面，也使其更難承受聲譽波動。第2季稅息折舊及攤銷前盈餘下降約12%至$3.45億，自然成長率下滑約0.6%，營收則增加約3%至$12.9億。S&P計算，若納入優先股，該公司2025年底槓桿率為盈餘的15.4倍；若不納入則約為9.6倍。公司所稱的過去12個月EBITDA為$16億，其中包含$8億加回項目，涵蓋預期節省成本、收購及其他調整。

管理層預期，營運重整與裁員可在2027年節省$3億。在效益真正實現以前，債券投資人仍須根據較弱的當期盈餘評估槓桿，而不能完全採信未來調整後的數字。價格下跌顯示，當資本結構本已依賴積極的盈餘假設，外部爭議可以非常迅速地放大市場疑慮。

澳洲Bathla Group面臨的則是更直接的私人信貸損失風險。這家雪梨房地產開發商進入破產程序，積欠貸款人約A$33億；公司一面尋求新資金，一面試圖讓專案繼續運作。約40家私人信貸公司曾為其融資，PAG、CVS Lane Capital Partners及Centuria Bass均為最大債權人之一，單是PAG的放款就超過A$3億。

Bathla陷入困境，是房價下跌、利率上升、營建成本增加與專案延誤共同作用的結果，而相關貸款市場又高度曝險於房地產開發。首次債權人會議訂於9月4日雪梨時間11:00舉行。當前關鍵問題是既有債權人是否願意提供額外資金、新資金可取得何種受償順位，以及損失將如何由分散的貸款人群體分攤。

## 主權與本地市場重新分配融資風險

塞內加爾出現最明顯的主權信用惡化。穆迪將其長期外幣評等由Caa1降至Caa2，並維持負向展望，理由是流動性風險嚴峻，且持續的融資壓力或債務處置，都提高了違約機率。2025年底中央政府債務接近GDP的117%，廣義公共部門債務則略高於130%。

塞內加爾2026年融資需求估計約占GDP的26%。前政府有$70億債務未曾揭露，此事曝光後，原有的$18億IMF計畫仍處於暫停狀態。IMF代表團目前正在達卡，但討論仍聚焦於就融資缺口規模及新計畫所需改革取得共識。

國內政治衝突使談判更為複雜。總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye於5月解除Ousmane Sonko的總理職務，但Sonko其後成為國民議會議長，其政黨仍掌握多數席次。Sonko反對債務重整，Faye則尚未承諾採行。塞內加爾任命Lazard擔任財務顧問，顯示政府正在研究不同選項，但尚未選定債務重整或重新安排到期結構。

巴西的壓力較集中於家庭部門，而非主權融資。7月個人貸款違約率由7.4%升至7.8%，創2009年以來最高；企業違約率則由4%升至4.2%。正式就業新增人數降至58,568人，低於以11.5萬人為中位數的調查中所有預估，也是2026年最疲弱的單月結果。

高昂借款成本正與政府擴大消費信貸的政策相互碰撞。7月個人貸款平均利率為60%，循環信用卡債務年利率則高達436.2%。即使政府債務協商計畫已重整逾R$220億債務，家庭債務占可支配所得的比率仍接近歷史高點。巴西央行最近一次會議將Selic利率下調25個基點至14%，但仍警告刺激消費可能使通膨持續高於目標。

中國境內債券市場吸引的，則是尋求顯著降低融資成本的借款人。UBS發行人民幣20億元、5年期熊貓債，票息1.78%；該行稱，這是同天期外資金融機構歷來最低利率與最窄利差。2026年熊貓債發行量已創人民幣2,140億元新高，較去年同期增加67%。

今年熊貓債平均票息較美元債低約200個基點。中國並將自9月起免收發行登記費，進一步降低成本。資本管制仍限制這個市場相對美國與歐洲所能扮演的角色，但相關交易為國際借款人提供另一項資金來源，也有助擴大人民幣使用。

市場為印度儲備銀行可能升息作準備之際，印度公司債曲線出現罕見倒掛。國營企業與銀行最高評級10年期債券的殖利率，逾一個月來首次低於同類3年期債券。8月3年期殖利率上升32個基點，10年期則上升22個基點，兩者利差由最高32個基點降至零以下。

發行人因而延長借款天期。Power Finance撤回較短天期發行案，同時為15年期債券定價；REC取消2年期發行，但繼續推進約10年期借款；Bajaj Finance則透過10年期票據籌得₹500億。退休金及公積金需求支撐長端，投資人則預期RBI即使啟動升息循環，總幅度也只會約50至75個基點。

台灣壽險業面臨較緩慢的結構調整，並將影響美元債需求。整體產業管理超過$1.2兆資產，海外持有部位逾$6,900億，其中約$1,620億為美國公司債。這些外國資產很大一部分用來支應新台幣負債，使保險公司承受幣別錯配風險。

金融監督管理委員會主委彭金隆要求業者設定年度目標，降低與本幣負債相關的外國資產曝險、增加國內投資，並擴大美元保單銷售。季度檢查現已納入海外配置，相關目標也與高階主管績效評估連結。惠譽預期，外國資產配置比率長期可能下降數個百分點，朝60%區間中段或低段移動。

這項轉變將循序漸進，因為台灣缺乏足夠多、規模又符合壽險需求的國內專案。政府希望3年內吸引NT$3,000億保險資金投入本地AI、半導體、基礎建設及長照投資，但業界主管表示，合適資產依然有限。儘管如此，這項政策仍為亞洲最大的機構買方群體之一帶來持續性理由，促使其放慢購買美國公司債與公債。

南非準備最快於截至2027年3月止財政年度首次發行綠色債券，以擴大主權債投資人基礎。政府估計，截至2035年，執行並資助氣候轉型需要約ZAR 3.7兆。最終規模、幣別與時程將在10月期中預算前後決定，並取決於合格專案供給與市場情勢。

該框架允許發行本幣、歐元或美元債，可用於電力輸送、水資源安全、再生能源基礎設施，以及協助勞工離開煤炭產業。南非希望在2030年前，每年從公共、民間、國內及國際來源籌得最多$80億。綠色債券形式可能吸引額外需求，但10月預算仍須說明這筆交易如何納入主權整體借款計畫。

## 後續市場意涵

美國公債曲線趨平後，第一項檢驗是即將公布的美國數據，能否證實投資人從華許談話中推斷出的政策急迫性。8月31日公布的達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數預計由-6升至-5，將顯示芝加哥PMI降至47.1，究竟是區域性現象，還是更廣泛景氣收縮的一部分。ISM製造業與服務業調查則會提供全國性的活動與支付價格指標，協助區分生產轉弱與投入成本通膨是否持續。

8月28日公布的就業基準修正下調民間就業歷史水準，9月4日就業報告則將反映當前勞動需求。經濟學家預期，非農就業在7月下降後將增加5.5萬人，失業率維持4.1%。接近預期的結果將支持華許對就業大致穩定的描述；更疲弱的數據則會提高升息代價，即使他的政策焦點仍在物價。

9月11日公布的8月CPI，是會議前最關鍵的通膨檢驗。華許表示，夏季較佳數據尚未形成具意義的趨勢，而市場已把9月升息機率推升至50%以上。若數據意外偏低，決策委員會可能重新選擇等待；基礎通膨若持續，則會強化7月已支持升息官員的理由。

聯準會9月15至16日的決策，將檢驗傑克森霍爾演說帶來的公信力效益。升息將證實主席提出的標準會轉化為行動，並延續週五的熊市趨平行情。若就業或通膨明顯轉弱，且華許能說明新資訊如何符合其政策框架，市場或可消化再次維持利率不變的結果；若按兵不動又缺少這項連結，7月後出現的長端拋售可能重演。

歐洲物價數據將更早出爐。德國通膨預計為3.1%，之後歐元區整體與核心通膨預計分別為3.3%及2.5%。若整體通膨由能源帶動、核心通膨維持穩定，將支持9月升息，但後續緊縮幅度仍有爭議。若漲勢更為廣泛，則會強化Dolenc的憂慮，即官員不能等到第二輪效應清楚浮現才採取行動。

日本下一輪政策訊號必須同時回答升息時點，以及9月之後的政策路徑。近期升息機率已超過80%，日圓已回吐匯市干預所帶來逾半升幅，2年期公債標售需求也相當疲弱。若只確認升息一次，對日圓的支撐可能有限；若有證據顯示正常化循環將持續，對JGB、日圓及日本投資人海外債券需求的影響都會更大。

日本預算程序另構成一項供給檢驗。各部會預算要求超過¥130兆，而高市希望把新發債控制在¥40兆以下；兩者要同時成立，稅收與非稅收入就必須符合樂觀假設，否則須削減支出。最終預算還必須吸收食品減稅提案約¥5兆的成本。後續標售將顯示，財政供給增加與日本央行收緊政策同時出現時，投資人要求多少價格讓利。

AI融資的考驗將來自最終條款，而非整體需求本身。SoftBank的銀行承諾期限為8月31日；新的$100億貸款、$400億過橋貸款、以OpenAI持股擔保的借款，以及潛在發債彼此如何安排，將決定還剩多少再融資與擔保品風險。Iren與Lambda必須在短天期GPU債務需要再融資前，將設備轉化為營運現金流；可轉換債市場則須在票息保障減少之際，吸收創紀錄發行量。

私人信貸結果將取決於債權人協調。Bathla在9月4日的會議必須釐清，貸款人是否願意為專案完工提供資金，以及任何新資金可取得何種順位。Acrisure則必須證明，其重整能把預估的2027年節省金額轉化為實際盈餘，而不過度依賴加回項目。塞內加爾方面，IMF代表團必須先就融資需求提出共同評估，新計畫或任何債務處置才可能取得可信度。

亞洲至亞洲時段稍後的一項發展，提高了圍繞上述政策檢驗的能源風險。週日美國固定收益市場收盤後，美軍攻擊準備在荷莫茲海峽部署水雷的伊朗火箭發射器，為數週來首次發動攻擊。事發後，布蘭特原油在亞洲早盤上漲1.9%至$89.75。這次升級並非週五美國公債走勢的成因，卻再次帶來能源價格可能干擾通膨數據與央行決策的風險，而這些因素正主導下一波利率調整。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off and the curve flattened sharply on Aug. 28 after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole address to say inflation was not slowing meaningfully, financial conditions were not restrictive and the Fed’s 2% objective remained firm. The 2-year yield rose 11.2 basis points to 4.345%, the 5-year climbed 8 basis points to 4.48%, the 10-year gained 4.3 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year added 1.2 basis points to 5.207%.

The concentration of the selloff at shorter maturities distinguished the session from the long-end weakness that followed Warsh’s July press conference. The 2s10s spread narrowed 6.9 basis points to 37.5 basis points and 2s30s compressed 10 basis points to 86.2. The 10-year real yield rose 5.8 basis points to 2.402%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 1.5 basis points to 2.318%. Investors therefore marked up the expected path of inflation-adjusted policy rates rather than demanding more inflation compensation across the full curve.

Warsh did not promise an increase at the Sept. 15-16 meeting. He described himself as committed to a policy discipline rather than a particular decision and retained his opposition to routine forward guidance. But his standard—that underlying inflation must be moving clearly toward 2% at sufficient speed—was more demanding than the message markets had taken from July. Federal-funds futures raised the probability of a September increase from around 36% before the speech to above 50%, while at least one move by year-end became nearly fully priced. Barclays shifted from expecting no increase in 2026 to forecasting quarter-point moves in September and December.

The repricing survived a set of weaker economic readings released around the speech. The Chicago purchasing managers’ index dropped to 47.1 in August from 57.6, far below the 58.3 consensus. The preliminary annual payroll benchmark reduced March employment by 79,000 rather than increasing it as economists had expected, with a substantially larger downgrade in private payrolls. University of Michigan sentiment remained below its July level, while near-term household inflation expectations were revised lower. Those releases kept the next decision conditional, but they did not displace Warsh’s judgment that current policy was not yet exerting enough restraint.

Cross-asset markets reflected the higher expected real-rate path. The Dollar Index rose 0.52%, while gold futures fell 2.85% to $4,478.10. The S&P 500 lost 0.27%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.71% and the semiconductor index dropped 3.48% as rate-sensitive technology shares gave back part of the previous session’s rally. The VIX nevertheless edged lower to 14.42, indicating an orderly repricing rather than a generalized rush for protection. WTI and Brent also declined modestly, limiting the day’s energy impulse, while investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market bond funds recorded small price losses.

The Treasury reaction addressed one source of long-end anxiety—doubt about the Fed’s inflation commitment—without removing the underlying demands on capital. US debt has passed $40 trillion, artificial-intelligence investment continues to produce large public and private financings, and long yields remain elevated even after the curve’s flattening. Abroad, weak demand at a Japanese 2-year auction, accelerating European inflation and idiosyncratic credit stress showed that tighter policy expectations are meeting heavy financing needs across several markets.

## Warsh Reprices the Policy Path as Growth Signals Weaken

Warsh’s most consequential change was not an explicit September call but a clearer description of the conditions that would justify restraint. He reaffirmed that the 2% target is defined through the personal consumption expenditures price index and is fixed, addressing concern created in July when he appeared to leave open the possibility of changing the inflation benchmark. He also said recent favorable CPI and PCE readings did not establish that the underlying trend had improved meaningfully.

His assessment of financial conditions supplied the stronger policy signal. By saying broad conditions were difficult to characterize as restrictive, Warsh challenged the argument that holding the federal-funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75% would gradually cool demand without another increase. He also called short-term interest rates the Fed’s predominant instrument for fulfilling its mandate, narrowing the ambiguity created by earlier discussion of multiple policy tools.

That framework aligned Warsh more closely with the officials who had already favored tighter policy. Three voting members dissented from the July decision in favor of a quarter-point increase, while several other officials supported a move and many said tightening would become necessary if inflation failed to decline. Warsh did not adopt their timing, but he elevated price stability above the case for waiting and described employment as broadly consistent with full employment.

The bond market supplied the missing conclusion. The 11.2-basis-point increase in the 2-year yield was the largest move among the benchmark tenors, while the 30-year barely rose. That pattern was consistent with an expected near-term policy response reducing some risk that inflation would remain uncontrolled farther into the future. The 2s30s curve’s 10-basis-point compression nearly matched the intraday flattening described after the speech.

Long maturities did not rally on a closing basis, however. The 30-year yield ended at 5.207%, still 11.7 basis points higher than a month earlier, while the 10-year was up 11.3 basis points over the same period. Fiscal borrowing, elevated energy costs and competition from corporate issuance continue to require substantial long-term compensation even if a more forceful Fed reduces one component of term premium.

Trading activity showed that the repricing occurred through an active cash market. FINRA recorded $1.17 trillion of nominal-coupon par activity, 19.1% more than on the previous day. Activity in maturities of 2 years or less rose 36.5%, while turnover in coupons longer than 5 years and no more than 7 years increased 30.3%. TIPS activity rose 84%. Those figures are two-way volumes rather than evidence of buyer or seller direction, but they locate the heaviest adjustment in the sectors most exposed to the policy reassessment.

The economic releases complicated, rather than reversed, that message. Chicago PMI’s fall to 47.1 marked an abrupt move from expansion to contraction and undershot every supplied comparison: 57.6 previously, a 58.3 consensus and a 56.1 forecast. The Dallas Fed manufacturing index on Aug. 31, expected at -5 after -6, becomes the next regional test of whether that weakness is localized or part of a broader industrial slowdown.

The payroll benchmark was less severe in aggregate than the previous annual adjustment but exposed a sharper private-sector slowdown. Total nonfarm employment for March was preliminarily revised down by 79,000, or 0.1%, compared with a prior annual revision of negative 911,000 and a survey expectation for an increase of 183,000. The latest adjustment was also smaller than the 0.2% average absolute revision over the previous decade.

Composition made the release more cautionary than the headline alone. Private employment was revised down by 178,000, including reductions of 67,000 in manufacturing and 98,000 in trade, transportation and utilities. Government employment was revised up by 99,000, offsetting much of the private downgrade in the total. The benchmark implies that average job growth in the year through March was closer to 11,000 a month than the previously reported 17,600. Final figures will be issued with the January 2027 employment report in February.

Consumer data also pointed to less momentum without providing an all-clear on inflation. Final August Michigan sentiment was 51.7, above the preliminary consensus of 51 but below July’s 55.2. One-year inflation expectations were revised down to 4% from 4.2%, against an expected 4.3%, but remained high. Five-year expectations held at 3.3%, matching the prior reading and consensus. Households were therefore less pessimistic than the preliminary survey suggested, yet neither confidence nor longer-term price expectations had returned to comfortable levels.

The weekly oil-rig count declined to 447 from 452, below the 454 consensus. That reduction does not determine immediate crude prices, but it preserves a medium-term supply concern at a time when the Middle East conflict remains the principal global energy risk. On Friday, WTI slipped 0.16% to $83.40 and Brent fell 0.43% to $89.31, offering modest near-term relief rather than a decisive change in the inflation backdrop.

The result is a policy path with greater market-implied urgency but no settled September outcome. The Chicago survey and private-payroll revision argue for caution, while the unchanged 5-year household inflation expectation and Warsh’s assessment of loose financial conditions leave tightening available. The risk of reversal is correspondingly high: if the Fed holds again without a clear explanation, the credibility doubts that steepened the curve in July could re-emerge.

## Japan’s Rate Expectations Strain Bonds and the Yen

Japanese markets delivered a parallel tightening signal through inflation, auction demand and currency policy. Tokyo consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 1.8% from a year earlier in August, up from 1.7% and matching expectations. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy reached 2%, while the overall index increased 1.9%. The acceleration occurred even as government measures reduced household energy costs.

The details showed services pressure alongside the subsidy effect. Service prices rose 1.4% from a year earlier, with rents, restaurant costs, medical fees and durable goods for education and recreation contributing. Food prices excluding fresh items increased 3.6%, although rice prices fell 14.2%, the largest decline since May 2005, after rising 68% a year earlier. Overall energy prices declined 2%; gasoline fell 2.7% and electricity 2.4% as the government capped fuel costs and subsidized electricity and gas from July through September.

Labor conditions remained tight. The unemployment rate declined to 2.4% in July, and the job-to-applicant ratio held at 1.18, indicating 118 available positions for every 100 applicants. The combination of sticky service inflation, labor scarcity and persistent yen weakness supported expectations for a Bank of Japan increase even though administered prices restrained the headline index.

That expectation was visible in the 2-year government-bond auction. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.97 from 3.63 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.74. The auction tail widened to 0.034 from 0.007, the broadest since 2016. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield had risen to 1.70% from about 1.56% at the start of August, while the 10-year approached 3% at 2.92%.

Overnight-index swaps placed the probability of a September BOJ increase at roughly 82% to 84%, with an October move fully priced. Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino had already warned that an upward deviation of underlying inflation from the 2% objective would damage the economy and had declined to push back against a September move. Weak auction demand showed that investors require either clearer guidance or additional price concession as that meeting approaches.

The Finance Ministry then disclosed the scale of its effort to support the currency. Japan spent ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, from July 30 through Aug. 26, a record for a one-month period. The campaign included coordinated US-Japanese intervention on July 31, the first joint operation to support the yen since 1998. The US amount was not included in Japan’s figures, but its participation increased the deterrent value of the action.

Intervention changed the path without correcting the underlying imbalance. The yen strengthened from nearly 164 per dollar before the first operation to 155.23 on Aug. 3, then weakened back to around 159.68 by Friday evening in Tokyo. Japan has spent about ¥27 trillion on intervention this year, yet the currency remains close to the 160 level. The wide US-Japan rate gap, elevated oil costs, fiscal concern and continued overseas investment by Japanese institutions are still working against sustained appreciation.

That leaves monetary policy doing more of the prospective work. A single September increase has already been heavily discounted, so a durable yen recovery would require confidence that normalization will continue beyond the next move. Warsh’s hawkish shift works in the opposite direction by raising the expected US rate path, limiting the currency benefit Japan might otherwise obtain from BOJ tightening.

Fiscal policy adds another source of pressure on JGB demand. Ministry budget requests for the next fiscal year could exceed a record ¥130 trillion, compared with about ¥125 trillion for the current initial and supplementary budgets combined. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has said she wants new bond issuance below ¥40 trillion, but the financing arithmetic is tight.

Tax revenue was projected at ¥87.8 trillion under a 3% nominal-growth assumption, up from an estimated ¥83.7 trillion this year. Takaichi’s planned consumption-tax cut on food would reduce receipts by about ¥5 trillion, bringing tax revenue back toward ¥83 trillion. Adding roughly ¥9 trillion of non-tax revenue would still leave a gap of almost ¥40 trillion if spending exceeds ¥130 trillion. Issuance near that level would be above the current fiscal year’s ¥32.7 trillion, even if it remained within the prime minister’s stated ceiling.

Corporate and foreign borrowers are also trying to secure yen funding before rates rise further. Japan’s hybrid issuance is expected to reach about ¥1.18 trillion through September, the most since fiscal 2021. Panasonic priced ¥100 billion of 30-year and 30-year-one-month subordinated bonds, with coupons of 3.455% and 4.188% and spreads of 110 and 130 basis points over JGBs. About ¥1.32 trillion of outstanding hybrids are expected to reach first-call dates during fiscal 2026, creating refinancing demand alongside acquisition financing.

Mexico raised ¥282.8 billion in its first Samurai offering in 2 years, compared with ¥152.2 billion in August 2024. Its four tranches ranged from 3.5 to 20 years and priced 115 to 210 basis points over yen swaps. The size of the transaction showed continued depth in Japan’s investor base, but the rush to borrow before additional BOJ action also adds to the supply investors must absorb.

## European Inflation Builds a Case for September Tightening

European inflation data and central-bank comments moved more uniformly toward higher rates. Spanish consumer prices rose 4.5% from a year earlier in August, the fastest pace since 2023 and more than double the European Central Bank’s objective. French inflation accelerated to 2.7%, its highest since May and above expectations. Energy linked to the Middle East conflict was the principal driver in both countries.

The euro-area reading due Sept. 1 is expected to show inflation rising to 3.3% from 2.9%, also the fastest since 2023. Core inflation is forecast to remain at 2.5%, which would indicate that the latest acceleration is still concentrated in energy rather than a broad new increase in underlying prices. Germany is expected at 3.1% and Italy at 3.4%.

Those figures will be the last major price readings before the ECB’s Sept. 10 decision. Investors are pricing another quarter-point increase after June’s initial move, which would lift the deposit rate to 2.5%. The remaining debate concerns whether that step is enough to prevent the energy shock from entering wages and other prices.

Slovenian central-bank Governor Primoz Dolenc said there was a strong case to act in September because economic growth had exceeded expectations, energy costs remained high and the Iran conflict had not improved significantly. He acknowledged that material second-round effects were not yet visible, but argued that waiting for them to emerge would risk a loss of confidence in the ECB’s target. If the bank increases rates in September, he sees the December projections as the next opportunity to reassess the medium-term path.

Latvian Governor Martins Kazaks likewise said elevated inflation could not be allowed to take root and described another increase as a considerable possibility. Austrian Governor Martin Kocher emphasized that the euro-area economy was showing more momentum than expected. Output grew 0.4% in Q2, allowing policymakers to consider additional restraint without evidence that the energy shock had already stopped growth.

The UK offered a notable contrast. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said second-round inflation effects remained subdued and the labor market had been softening, allowing officials to watch the situation for now. He had voted with the 6-3 majority to hold rates on July 30 and warned at the time against interpreting that decision as movement toward an increase.

Markets nevertheless fully priced a quarter-point BOE increase by year-end and another by spring. UK inflation had accelerated for the first time since March, and households’ expected price increase over the coming year reached 3.9%. Bailey’s counterweight was the weakness in employment: companies were shedding workers, vacancies were at a 5-year low and private-sector wage growth was slowing. He did not promise that subdued second-round effects would persist, leaving the Sept. 17 decision dependent on whether energy inflation spreads into pay and services.

France combines the regional inflation problem with a more difficult sovereign-credit backdrop. Revised figures showed output contracted 0.2% in Q1 and stagnated in Q2, leaving the economy narrowly short of recession. At the same time, the 10-year French yield premium over Germany has widened to about 85 basis points from less than 60 at the start of 2026.

The first presidential debate exposed little agreement on how to narrow the deficit. Jean-Luc Mélenchon defended negotiating cancellation of debt held by the ECB, while Marine Le Pen proposed shrinking the state, reducing immigration and possibly cutting EU contributions to save €125 billion. Le Pen also retained a pension proposal that could allow retirement from age 60 and cost about €9 billion annually. Former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe rejected debt cancellation as a threat to France’s financing access.

Fitch left France’s rating at A+ with a stable outlook, giving the government a reprieve but preserving explicit downgrade risks. The agency said continued political fragmentation or failure to make substantial progress on deficit reduction could lead first to a negative outlook and then to a lower rating. It forecasts deficits of 5.2% of GDP in 2026, 5.5% in 2027 and 5.2% in 2028, worse than its previous assessment because of weaker growth, higher interest costs and greater defense spending.

The combination of rising ECB rates and fiscal gridlock leaves France unusually exposed within the euro area. September tightening may address regional inflation, but it also raises the cost of carrying deficits that Fitch expects to remain above 5% through 2028. The stable rating prevents an immediate ratings shock; it does not resolve the premium investors already demand for domestic political and budget risk.

## AI Financing Expands as Credit Protection Erodes

Artificial-intelligence investment continues to draw on nearly every part of the debt market. Pimco attributed part of the rise in the 10-year Treasury yield toward 4.75% earlier in August to a rapid flood of AI-related issuance competing with government borrowing. The investment cycle may improve productivity and growth, but the near-term requirement is large amounts of capital at a time when sovereign financing needs are also rising.

SoftBank is seeking another $10 billion, 2-year loan priced around 275 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate. Mizuho is arranging the facility, for which bank commitments are due Aug. 31. Proceeds could refinance part of the $40 billion bridge loan used to fund the company’s OpenAI investment.

The new borrowing sits alongside a possible bond sale of as much as $20 billion and an existing $10 billion loan secured by SoftBank’s OpenAI stake, with covenants that can require cash collateral or early repayment. SoftBank is due to invest close to $65 billion in OpenAI by October. Access to several markets reduces dependence on any one investor group, but the bank loan, secured borrowing and potential bonds all finance the same concentrated technology exposure.

Lambda raised about $1 billion of short-dated private debt to buy Nvidia graphics processors that will be leased to Microsoft. JPMorgan arranged the placement. The transaction followed a separate $926 million loan completed earlier in August for GPUs and related infrastructure. Lambda’s Microsoft agreement supplies a known user for the equipment, but the financing still depends on the value, utilization and technological life of specialized chips.

Iren obtained an even larger and more expensive package. Blue Owl funds led a $2.4 billion financing consisting of a $1.2 billion senior-secured term loan and $1.2 billion of senior-secured notes. Both portions carry a 9% rate and mature 2½ years after funding. The structure allows Iren to purchase Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs in stages for its Canadian data-center campus.

The short maturity is significant because Iren forecast as much as $30 billion of capital expenditure in its 2027 financial year. Staged purchases reduce immediate funding needs, but they do not remove refinancing risk if construction, customer demand or GPU economics change before the debt matures. Iren’s shares fell almost 13% on Friday after its earnings release.

Convertible issuance shows investors accepting a different form of reduced protection. Global technology-company convertible sales have reached $147 billion this year, more than 50% above the same point in 2025 and already above the previous annual record set in 2021. Some new coupons have moved toward zero as buyers rely increasingly on the option to convert into equity for their return.

The average delta of the convertible market, measuring sensitivity to the underlying shares, has risen to about 64%, near its highest since 2021. Nebius alone raised $4.5 billion last week after having previously issued another $9.75 billion; part of the new transaction carried a coupon between 0% and 0.5%. The low income cushion means a fall in the issuer’s equity can leave holders with unsecured debt that provides little current return.

This does not reproduce the 2021 market exactly. Several current issuers have stronger revenue growth and profitability than the companies that sold zero-coupon convertibles during the pandemic. It does, however, concentrate equity, credit and convertible portfolios in the same AI theme. The distinction between an expanding productive industry and an overfinanced one will depend on project utilization, borrower cash flow and how much protection survives in the final documentation.

Not all credit stress is related to new AI construction. Acrisure’s $4.4 billion loan due in 2030 fell about 10 points during August to roughly 83 cents, the largest negative contribution among borrowers in the Bloomberg US Leveraged Loan Index. Its $1.1 billion of 2030 bonds traded as low as about 87 cents and became the second-largest monthly drag on a broad US high-yield index.

Concern about Acrisure’s connection to Guggenheim compounded weaker operating results and high leverage. Guggenheim Investments participated for clients in a 2022 preferred-equity financing, although Acrisure said attempts to portray that minority investment as a broader relationship were misleading. The association has nevertheless attracted attention as US authorities examine potential improprieties elsewhere in Mark Walter’s financial complex.

Acrisure’s own fundamentals leave less room for reputational volatility. Q2 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization fell about 12% to $345 million, organic growth declined roughly 0.6%, and revenue rose about 3% to $1.29 billion. S&P calculated leverage at 15.4 times earnings at the end of 2025 when preferred equity was included, or about 9.6 times without it. The company’s $1.6 billion measure of trailing EBITDA included $800 million of addbacks for expected savings, acquisitions and other adjustments.

Management expects an operational overhaul and workforce reduction to produce $300 million of savings in 2027. Until those benefits are realized, debt investors must evaluate leverage against weaker current earnings rather than the full prospective adjustment. The price declines show how quickly an external controversy can amplify concern when the capital structure already relies on aggressive earnings assumptions.

Australia’s Bathla Group represents a more direct private-credit loss risk. The Sydney property developer entered insolvency owing lenders about A$3.3 billion and is seeking new capital while trying to keep projects operating. Roughly 40 private-credit firms have helped finance it, with PAG, CVS Lane Capital Partners and Centuria Bass among the largest lenders. PAG’s extensions alone exceed A$300 million.

Bathla’s distress combines falling home prices, higher rates, rising construction costs and delayed projects in a lending market heavily exposed to real-estate development. Its first creditor meeting is scheduled for Sept. 4 at 11:00 Sydney time. The immediate questions are whether existing creditors will provide additional money, what priority that capital receives and how losses are divided across a fragmented lender group.

## Sovereign and Local Markets Redistribute Funding Risk

Senegal suffered the clearest sovereign-credit deterioration. Moody’s downgraded its long-term foreign-currency rating to Caa2 from Caa1 and retained a negative outlook, citing acute liquidity risk and a greater probability of default through either persistent funding strain or a debt treatment. Central-government debt stood near 117% of GDP at the end of 2025, while broader public-sector debt was slightly above 130%.

The country faces 2026 financing needs estimated at about 26% of GDP. Its previous $1.8 billion IMF program remains suspended following the discovery of $7 billion of debt that had not been disclosed by the former administration. An IMF mission is in Dakar, but discussions are still focused on agreeing the scale of the financing gap and the reforms needed for a new program.

Domestic political conflict complicates that negotiation. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye dismissed Ousmane Sonko as prime minister in May, but Sonko subsequently became speaker of the National Assembly, where his party retains a majority. Sonko opposes restructuring, while Faye has not committed to one. Senegal’s appointment of Lazard as financial adviser indicates that options are being studied, but neither restructuring nor reprofiling has been selected.

Brazil’s stress is concentrated more in households than in sovereign funding. The personal-loan default rate rose to 7.8% in July from 7.4%, its highest since 2009, while the corporate rate increased to 4.2% from 4%. Formal job creation slowed to 58,568, below every estimate in a survey centered on 115,000 and the weakest monthly result of 2026.

High borrowing costs are colliding with a government effort to expand consumer credit. The average rate on personal loans was 60% in July, while revolving credit-card debt cost 436.2% annually. Household debt relative to disposable income remains near a record, even after a government renegotiation program restructured more than 22 billion reais. The central bank cut the Selic rate by 25 basis points to 14% at its latest meeting but continues to warn that consumption stimulus could keep inflation above target.

China’s onshore bond market is attracting borrowers seeking the opposite condition: materially cheaper financing. UBS sold 2 billion yuan of 5-year panda bonds at a 1.78% coupon, which it described as the lowest rate and tightest spread for a foreign financial institution of that maturity. Panda issuance has reached a record 214 billion yuan in 2026, 67% more than in the same period last year.

Average panda coupons are about 200 basis points below dollar-bond coupons this year. China will waive issuance registration fees beginning in September, further reducing costs. Capital controls still limit the market’s role relative to the US and Europe, but the transactions provide international borrowers with an additional funding base while promoting wider use of the yuan.

India’s corporate curve has developed an unusual inversion as markets prepare for possible Reserve Bank tightening. Yields on top-rated 10-year debt from state-owned companies and banks fell below comparable 3-year yields for the first time in more than a month. Three-year yields rose 32 basis points during August, compared with 22 basis points for 10-year debt, and the gap moved from as wide as 32 basis points to below zero.

Issuers responded by extending maturity. Power Finance withdrew a shorter offering while pricing 15-year debt, REC canceled a 2-year sale while proceeding with roughly 10-year borrowing, and Bajaj Finance raised 50 billion rupees through 10-year notes. Pension and provident-fund demand is supporting the long end, while investors expect any RBI hiking cycle to be limited to about 50 to 75 basis points.

Taiwan’s insurers face a slower structural adjustment with implications for dollar bonds. The industry manages more than $1.2 trillion and holds over $690 billion overseas, including roughly $162 billion in US corporate debt. Much of that foreign portfolio backs Taiwan-dollar liabilities, leaving the insurers exposed to currency mismatches.

Financial Supervisory Commission Chair Peng Jin-lung is requiring annual targets to reduce foreign exposure associated with local-currency liabilities, increase domestic investment and expand sales of US-dollar policies. Quarterly reviews now monitor overseas allocations, and the targets are being linked to senior executives’ performance assessments. Fitch expects foreign-asset allocations could decline by several percentage points toward the mid- or low-60% range over time.

The shift will be gradual because Taiwan lacks enough domestic projects of the scale insurers require. The government aims to attract NT$300 billion of insurance money into local AI, semiconductor, infrastructure and long-term-care investments over 3 years, but industry executives say suitable assets remain limited. The policy nevertheless introduces a persistent reason for one of Asia’s largest institutional buyer groups to slow purchases of US corporate bonds and Treasuries.

South Africa is preparing to broaden its sovereign investor base with a debut green bond as early as the fiscal year ending March 2027. The government estimates that implementing and financing its climate transition will require about 3.7 trillion rand through 2035. The final size, currency and timing will be decided around October’s midterm budget and will depend on the availability of qualifying projects and market conditions.

The framework allows domestic, euro- or dollar-denominated issuance and could fund electricity transmission, water security, renewable-energy infrastructure and support for workers leaving the coal sector. South Africa hopes to raise as much as $8 billion annually by 2030 from public, private, domestic and international sources. A green format may attract additional demand, but the October budget must still establish how the transaction fits within the sovereign’s wider borrowing program.

## Forward Market Significance

The first test of the Treasury flattening is whether upcoming US data validate the urgency investors inferred from Warsh. The Aug. 31 Dallas Fed manufacturing index is expected at -5 after -6 and will show whether Chicago PMI’s fall to 47.1 is part of a broader regional contraction. The ISM manufacturing and services surveys will add national measures of activity and prices paid, separating weaker production from any persistence in input inflation.

The Aug. 28 payroll benchmark lowered the historical level of private employment, but the Sept. 4 jobs report will address the current state of labor demand. Economists expect payrolls to rise by 55,000 after July’s decline and unemployment to remain at 4.1%. A result near that forecast would support Warsh’s description of employment as broadly steady; a weaker release would increase the cost of tightening despite his focus on prices.

August CPI on Sept. 11 is the decisive pre-meeting inflation test. Warsh said better summer data had not yet established a meaningful trend, and the market moved the probability of a September increase above 50%. A downside surprise could return the committee to waiting, while persistent underlying inflation would strengthen the case of officials who already favored an increase in July.

The Fed’s Sept. 15-16 decision will then test the credibility benefit produced by Jackson Hole. A hike would extend Friday’s bear flattening by confirming that the chair’s standard leads to action. Another hold could be absorbed if employment or inflation weakens clearly and Warsh explains how that information satisfies his framework. A hold without such a bridge risks reviving the long-end selloff that followed July.

European price data arrive sooner. Germany is expected to report 3.1% inflation, followed by a 3.3% euro-area headline rate and 2.5% core reading. Energy-led acceleration with stable core inflation would support a September increase while leaving the extent of later tightening debatable. A broader rise would reinforce Dolenc’s concern that officials cannot wait for visible second-round effects before acting.

Japan’s next policy signals must address both timing and the path beyond September. A near-term BOJ increase is already priced at more than 80%, the yen has surrendered over half of its intervention-driven gain, and the 2-year auction showed weak demand. Confirmation of only one move may provide limited currency support; evidence of a continuing normalization cycle would have larger consequences for JGBs, the yen and Japanese demand for overseas bonds.

The Japanese budget process adds a separate supply test. Ministry requests above ¥130 trillion and Takaichi’s goal of keeping new issuance below ¥40 trillion can coexist only if tax and non-tax revenue meet optimistic assumptions or spending is reduced. The final budget must also absorb the roughly ¥5 trillion cost of the proposed food-tax cut. Subsequent auctions will show how much concession investors require as fiscal supply and BOJ tightening converge.

AI financing will be tested through completed terms rather than aggregate demand alone. SoftBank’s bank commitments are due Aug. 31, with the relationship among the new $10 billion facility, its $40 billion bridge loan, secured OpenAI borrowing and possible bond sale determining how much refinancing and collateral risk remains. Iren and Lambda must convert short-dated GPU debt into operating cash flow before refinancing becomes necessary, while the convertible market must absorb record issuance with less coupon protection.

Private-credit outcomes will depend on creditor coordination. Bathla’s Sept. 4 meeting must establish whether lenders will fund project completion and what priority any new money receives. Acrisure must demonstrate that its restructuring can turn projected 2027 savings into realized earnings without relying excessively on addbacks. In Senegal, the IMF mission must produce a common financing assessment before a new program or any debt treatment can become credible.

A later development during the Asia-to-Asia window raised the energy risk around all of these policy tests. On Sunday, after the US fixed-income close, the US military struck Iranian rocket launchers preparing to deploy mines in the Strait of Hormuz, its first attack in weeks. Brent rose 1.9% to $89.75 in early Asian trading after the strike. The escalation did not cause Friday’s Treasury move, but it reopens the possibility that energy prices will complicate the inflation releases and central-bank decisions now governing the next rates adjustment.

Elevated sovereign borrowing, AI financing and overseas tightening pressures continued to support long-term yields.

Borrowers turned to China’s cheaper panda market, and Indian issuers extended maturities as the corporate curve inverted. Taiwan’s insurers face pressure to reduce foreign exposure, potentially slowing purchases of US bonds, while South Africa is preparing a debut green bond to broaden its funding base.

US labor and inflation data will determine whether Warsh’s stricter standard leads to a Sept. 15-16 increase or permits another hold without reviving credibility concerns. overall_summary.headline: Treasury yields rise and the curve flattens sharply after Warsh shifts policy expectations higher
overall_summary.session_narrative:
At the Aug. 28 NY close, Treasury yields rose most sharply at shorter maturities: the 2-year climbed 11.2 basis points to 4.345%, the 5-year rose 8 basis points to 4.48%, the 10-year gained 4.3 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year added 1.2 basis points to 5.207%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 6.9 basis points to 37.5 basis points, while 2s30s compressed 10 basis points to 86.2.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation was not slowing meaningfully, financial conditions were not restrictive and the 2% objective remained firm. The 10-year real yield rose 5.8 basis points while the breakeven rate declined 1.5 basis points, indicating that investors raised the expected path of inflation-adjusted policy rates rather than demanding more inflation compensation. Futures lifted the probability of a September increase from around 36% to above 50%.

Chicago PMI’s drop to 47.1, a 79,000 downward payroll benchmark revision and still-weak consumer sentiment preserved uncertainty but did not reverse the policy repricing. Abroad, weak demand at Japan’s 2-year bond auction, accelerating European inflation and expanding AI-related financing showed tighter policy expectations colliding with heavy public and private funding needs.
